analysis.summary: The PR migrates the infrastructure to SST v2, but introduces functional regressions in BFF logic and API parameter handling that will likely cause runtime failures.

bugs.title: Endpoint fetching disabled in Cart Price Details BFF
bugs.description: The 'fetchEndpoints' property has been changed from 'true' to 'false' in the BFF wrapper configuration. This prevents the endpoint directory from being fetched and injected into the handler.
bugs.risk: High. BFFs (Backend-for-Frontend) like 'cart-price-details' rely on the endpoint directory to communicate with commerce backends. Disabling this fetch will cause the handler to receive 'undefined' for endpoint configurations, leading to runtime crashes when attempting to call external services.
bugs.codeSnippet:
{
     auth: false,
-    fetchEndpoints: true,
+    fetchEndpoints: false,
     schema: {queryParams: QueryParams},

bugs.title: Parameter mismatch in getPriceDetails utility call
bugs.description: The argument passed to 'getPriceDetails' was changed from the full 'response' object to the inner 'response-data' property. However, there is no corresponding change to the utility's definition.
bugs.risk: High. If 'getPriceDetails' expects the full response wrapper (as indicated by the previous code), it will now fail to find its required properties on the nested data object, likely resulting in 'undefined' attributes or a runtime TypeError.

notBugs.reason: The removal of 'rotatingVerifySecret' across all BFFs and the Feature App is consistent and appears to be an intentional migration towards SST's Config/Secret management.
Deleting keys while iterating over Object.entries is safe in JavaScript as it iterates over a snapshot of the keys, and this pattern is standard for normalizing header case.
While this looks like a scope violation, moving the integrator into the feature app entry point is a common pattern for 'sst dev' workflows to enable standalone local development.
